handbookNote: New York Real Property Law (RPL) Article 12-A, "Real Estate Brokers and Real Estate Salespersons" (Sections 440 through 443-a -- definitions, licensing, application/education/exam requirements, fees, revocation/suspension/discipline, commission-splitting, nonresident reciprocity, the State Real Estate Board, and the agency-relationship disclosure form), together with related statutes RPL Article 8 Section 242 (utility/gas-well disclosure), RPL Article 9 Section 333-c (agricultural district disclosure), RPL Article 14 Sections 460-467 ("Property Condition Disclosure Act"), Executive Law Article 15 Section 296(5) (Human Rights Law unlawful discriminatory practices) and 42 USC 3604 (federal Fair Housing Act), and the implementing rules of the NY Department of State, Division of Licensing Services at 19 NYCRR Subchapter D: Part 175 (Regulations Affecting Brokers and Salespersons), Part 176 (Approval of Real Estate Courses, including the official 77-hour salesperson qualifying-course syllabus), Part 177 (Continuing Education), Part 178 (Nonsolicitation Orders), and Part 179 (Determination of Real Estate Experience) -- sourced from the NY DOS "Real Estate License Law" booklet (March 2026 edition) and DOS's public real-estate-agent licensing page; exam mechanics confirmed directly from DOS (multiple choice, 1.5-hour time limit, based on the 77-hour pre-licensing curriculum, pass/fail-only score reporting, $15 exam fee, 2-year validity of a passing result) -- DOS's own materials do not publish an exact item count or passing percentage (consistent with their pass/fail-only reporting policy); the commonly-cited 75-question/70%-passing figures are third-party test-prep-source estimates, not DOS-confirmed, and are flagged as such within the question bank -- price set to $29.99 per user instruction (2026-08-13), applies to all Real Estate tracks not yet loaded into D1
